result.title: Learning through Capacity Awareness to Minimize Hospital Readmissions
result.summary: Predictive algorithms are increasingly used to guide hospital discharge decisions, yet these models can exhibit censoring bias for vulnerable patients due to insufficient historical data or past discharge decisions. When biased readmission risk predictors are used to inform discharges, the training data generated by discharge decisions may perpetuate similar biases when predictors are re-trained, leading to a vicious cycle. We extend a queueing-based Markov decision process for hospital discharge to incorporate periodically retrained readmission risk predictors. Our key insight is that cost-optimal, "capacity-aware" operational decision policies can naturally diversify the lengths of stay at which patient outcomes are observed, enabling consistent estimation of readmission risk without explicit fairness constraints. We prove that repeated retraining under discharge-up-to policies converges to unbiased risk estimates under well-specification. In synthetic experiments and calibrated simulations based on patient-level data from a partner hospital, we find that where commonly used threshold-on-risk policies can remain persistently biased, discharge-up-to policies reduce learning error over status quo decision policies (such as thresholding on risk) by 24%-25%. These improvements to estimation also mitigate some forms of bias, reducing readmission cost disparities (adjusted for baseline risk differences between demographic groups) by 38%-63%. Our results demonstrate how capacity-aware decision policies can improve both predictive performance and fairness by addressing censoring bias.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将医院出院决策建模为基于排队的 MDP，并纳入需定期重训的再入院风险预测器，证明「容量感知」的 discharge-up-to 策略可通过让住院时长多样化来消除删失偏差、在模型规范正确时收敛到无偏风险估计，并在合成实验与校准仿真中降低学习误差和再入院成本差异。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心机制「决策策略决定结果在何处被观测、进而改变后续训练的监督分布与反馈回环」，可能与 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、推理轨迹的监督与贡献分配所面临的分布偏移问题在概念上相通，可供核查，但属于远域类比。
